category_title: Proactive Korean international students who voice ideas and hold ground in group discussions
scenario_title: Withdrawing from group discussion when faced with stubborn peers
minimal_context: The student is participating in a Marketing Management II seminar and is expected to share their reading analysis with their diverse project group.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time to work on the Marketing Management II group project. Please go ahead and share your ideas on the readings with your group members.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Could you look at my work first? With my assignments, I still try to receive the instructor’s feedback; so when I share my work with others, I have the right answers.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: The goal of the seminar is to discuss the readings together. You should just share what you have with them now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I feel a sense of responsibility to act as a model student so that other members do not look down upon Korean students. I am very conscious of their evaluation of my performance.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try to convince them to accept your ideas. What did they say when you started the discussion?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: With peers who are stubborn and defensive, I rarely say anything because I don’t want to bring negativity to the group. I just lost my self-confidence and withdrew from group participation before even attempting to convince others.
